title: Slow-cooker white chicken chilli
subtitle: Creamy, gently spiced chilli with chicken and white beans
excerpt: Chicken thighs and cannellini beans in a creamy, green-chilli-spiced broth. Mild enough for most palates, warming enough for winter. A very good alternative to the red kind.
sourceNotes: White chicken chilli is an American dish popularised in the southwestern United States from the 1980s. It uses white beans and green chillies rather than the red tomato base of traditional chilli con carne.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Defrost overnight in the fridge and reheat gently. The cream cheese may separate slightly; stir well when reheating.
recipe.batchNotes: Good batch-cook recipe. The flavour improves after a day in the fridge.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the day before and refrigerate. Add the cream cheese when reheating.

content.text: White chilli gets its colour and its character from green chillies and white beans rather than the red tomato base of the original. The cream cheese goes in at the end, not the start, which keeps it from splitting. Stir it in during the last 30 minutes or once the chilli is off the heat.
This is a mild dish by default. The green chilli adds flavour rather than heat. Add chilli flakes at the end if you want more bite.
Serve with tortilla chips, rice, or cornbread. Soured cream and spring onion are good toppings.

Add {{chicken-thighs-boneless}} of chicken thighs to the slow cooker. Add {{cannellini-beans}} of drained cannellini beans, {{chilli-green}} green chillies, {{onion}} diced onion, and {{garlic}} of crushed garlic. Add {{cumin-ground}} of cumin, {{coriander-ground}} of coriander, and {{oregano-dried}} of oregano. Pour over {{stock-chicken}} of chicken stock. Season with {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt.

Set the slow cooker to LOW and cook for 5 to 6 hours. Lift the chicken out and shred with two forks. Return to the pot. Stir in {{cream-cheese}} of cream cheese in small spoonfuls. Switch to HIGH and cook for 15 minutes until the cream cheese has melted into the broth. Squeeze in {{lime}} lime juice. Top with fresh coriander if using.

rows.symptom: The cream cheese has split and looks grainy
rows.cause: Cream cheese can split if stirred in when the temperature is too high.
rows.fix: Stir vigorously with a whisk. A splash of warm water can help bring it back. Next time stir the cream cheese in when the heat is reduced, not when the pot is at full temperature.

rows.cause: Green chillies vary widely in heat and flavour. Some are very mild.
rows.fix: Add the juice of the lime, which immediately brightens the flavour. A pinch of chilli flakes and more cumin also help.

rows.cause: The stock and beans together created more liquid than expected.
rows.fix: Mash a third of the beans directly in the pot to thicken. Or cook on HIGH with the lid off for 20 minutes.

rows.cause: Boneless thighs can dry out if cooked on HIGH for too long.
rows.fix: Keep to LOW at 5 to 6 hours maximum. Stir the shredded meat well through the creamy broth so it re-absorbs liquid.

content.text: White chicken chilli came out of the American southwest in the 1980s as a lighter, creamier alternative to beef chilli. It became widely popular across the United States and reached British kitchens later. The slow cooker version is now one of the most-made variations at home. It is an excellent weeknight dish and freezes well.
